platforms.name: Riachuelo-class (Scorpène BR)

propulsion.notes: Stretched hull (70.62m vs standard 61.7m Scorpène) — extra volume for batteries instead of MESMA AIP

sensors.sonar: Thales TSM 2233 Eledone (hull + flank passive array)

operators.notes: S-40 Riachuelo (commissioned Sep 2022), S-41 Humaitá (Jan 2024), S-42 Tonelero (sea trials 2025), S-43 Angostura (launched Nov 2025)

platforms.notes: PROSUB program ($9.3B total including infrastructure). Largest variant of Scorpène design at 70.62m. Brazilian-built at Itaguaí Naval Base shipyard. Technology transfer from Naval Group. No AIP — extended battery capacity instead. Built alongside nuclear submarine program.

platforms.name: SN-10 Álvaro Alberto (Nuclear SSN)

propulsion.notes: Entirely indigenous Brazilian reactor design by CTMSP. Non-nuclear systems by Naval Group. First steel cut June 2024. Brazil will become 7th nation with nuclear submarines.

operators.notes: Expected commissioning 2032-2034. Under construction at Itaguaí

platforms.notes: PROSUB program Phase 2. Most specs are estimated/speculative. Reactor is entirely Brazilian design (CTMSP/Centro Tecnológico da Marinha em São Paulo). Naval Group contracted for non-nuclear hull/systems integration. 100m hull, ~6,000t submerged. Will make Brazil 7th nuclear submarine nation. Originally designated S-N Álvaro Alberto, now SN-10.
